context_requirements: Active SRC-family kinase signaling, ideally with elevated SRC/FAK phosphorylation or SRC amplification
Co-activation of receptor tyrosine kinases such as EGFR, HER2, or MET that signal through SRC
Adherent epithelial or mesenchymal tumor cells with intact integrin/FAK adhesion signaling
Proliferating cells dependent on SRC-driven survival or cell-cycle progression
falsifiers: No decrease in SRC/FAK pathway-associated transcripts or SRC target genes at 6 or 24 h in any line
No antiproliferative or apoptosis-associated transcriptional signature at 24 h in lines with active SRC signaling
Strong and uniform upregulation of immediate-early or stress genes across all nine lines, indicating nonspecific toxicity rather than SRC inhibition
Lack of any differential response between lines with high SRC activation (e.g., HT29, A549) and low SRC-dependency lines

evidence.supports: Dasatinib, a Src inhibitor, inhibits breast cancer cell growth and modulates EGFR/Akt/Erk signaling, supporting SRC as a target in breast cancer lines such as MCF7.
AZD0530 Src inhibitor downregulates Src, FAK, p-FAK, p-paxillin, p-STAT3, and XIAP in sensitive pancreatic tumors, indicating SRC pathway suppression as a proximal effect.
Saracatinib (AZD0530) activity in colorectal cancer correlates with Src/FAK activation, supporting context-dependent response in lines such as HT29.
Dasatinib, a dual Abl/Src inhibitor, inactivates Bcr/Abl, STAT5, and ERK1/2 and downregulates Bcl-xL and Mcl-1, linking SRC inhibition to apoptosis and survival signaling.
KX2-391, a Src inhibitor, shows clinical activity in solid tumors including prostate and pancreas, supporting potential responsiveness in PC3 and VCAP lines.
